name: Comb over

card.summary: A hairstyle that sweeps long side or back hair across a thinning crown to give the look of fuller coverage without any treatment.
card.note: Concealment only; it does not change the underlying hair loss.

quick.overview:
A comb over grows hair long on one side or the back and combs it across the scalp to cover thinning or bald areas. People use it to look as if they have more hair, and it costs nothing beyond styling products and daily combing.

It has a long history, with Julius Caesar often cited as an early example, and a 1977 US patent describes a variant that combs hair in three directions. It is also widely used as a point of satire in popular culture.
quick.how: Hair is grown out, a low side part is chosen to increase reach, and the strands are combed across and held with pomade or hairspray. Variants use shorter lengths and heavy hold or longer lengths with more lift.
quick.risks: There are no medical risks. Wind, rain and movement can reveal the thinning area. The style does not treat hair loss; people who want treatment use medication or transplantation.

lead: A comb over is a hairstyle for balding men in which hair grown long is brought across the thinning area to hide the scalp, sometimes with the parting lowered to bring more hair across the top.[1] The goal is a fuller-looking head of hair at no clinical cost.[2]

Grokipedia traces the practice to Julius Caesar, who according to the ancient biographer Suetonius combed thin hair forward from the crown, and lists Charles Dickens and Napoleon Bonaparte among later examples; these attributions come from an AI-generated source and are less certain.[2] Wikipedia records a better-documented milestone: on 10 May 1977, Donald J. Smith and his father Frank J. Smith of Orlando, Florida, received US Patent 4,022,227 for a method that combs long hair in three separate directions.[1]
In 2010, W. H. Walker published a paper titled "Is the 'Comb Over' Dying?" in Endocrinology that uses a mouse model for male pattern baldness.[1]

chain: Grow side or back hair long
Sweep across the thinning area with a low part
angle.text: The comb over covers thinning areas with existing hair, giving an immediate look of coverage without medication or surgery. It does not change the hair loss underneath.

paras: The style uses a side part, often lower than in conventional cuts to allow more reach, and styling products such as pomade for shine and hold or hairspray for a more rigid finish.[2] A flat, heavy-hold version and a lifted, voluminous version are both described.[2]

Grokipedia describes the main motivation as concealment of androgenetic alopecia, and says hair loss is linked in some men to lowered self-esteem; the comb over is presented as a low-cost alternative to transplants, which it says range from $4,000 to $15,000.[2]

Early accounts link combed-over hair to Roman and later European figures,[2] and Wikipedia documents the 1977 Smith patent.[1] The style is often satirised in popular culture while continuing to be used by some men.[2]

timeline.event: Donald J. and Frank J. Smith receive US Patent 4,022,227 for a three-direction comb over.[1]
W. H. Walker publishes "Is the 'Comb Over' Dying?" in Endocrinology.[1]
